title: Fixed width and height cause horizontal and vertical overflow on small screens
claim: The #game-container has fixed width:800px and height:600px, which are not overridden in the max-width:600px media query, causing the layout to overflow on mobile devices.
evidence: Lines 20-21 set width:800px and height:600px. In the @media (max-width:600px) block (lines 180-183), only margin and padding are changed; width and height remain fixed.
trigger: Viewing the game on a viewport narrower than 800px or shorter than 600px.
impact: Horizontal scroll bars appear, content may be cut off, and the game is not fully visible without zooming.
test_implication: Responsive testing on mobile viewports should verify that the game container fits within the viewport.
suggested_verification: Open the page in a browser with viewport width 600px or less and observe overflow.
suggested_fix: In the media query, set width:auto or width:100%, max-width:800px, and height:auto (or use responsive units like vh/vw).

title: Absolute positioning with only top specified leads to unpredictable placement; responsive bottom/left/right overrides are ineffective
claim: #player-info is absolutely positioned with top:50% and transform:translateY(-50%) but no left/right, so it is placed at the static position (likely left edge) and vertically centered. In the media query, bottom:10px, left:10px, right:10px are set, but top:50% remains, so those bottom/left/right values are ignored, and the panel does not anchor to the bottom as intended.
evidence: Lines 86-88 set position:absolute; top:50%; transform:translateY(-50%) but omit left/right. In @media (max-width:600px), lines 192-197 add bottom:10px; left:10px; right:10px; without overriding top or setting top:auto.
trigger: Viewing the game on any screen, especially small screens where the intended bottom placement is expected.
impact: The player info panel may overlap other elements unpredictably and does not respect the responsive positioning, leading to a broken layout.
test_implication: Visual inspection of the player info panel placement across screen sizes is required.
suggested_verification: Resize the browser to below 600px and observe where the player info appears; compare with the intended bottom-left/right anchored design.
suggested_fix: Set default left/right (e.g., left:0; right:0; margin:auto) or use a non-absolute layout. In the media query, add top:auto; bottom:10px; and remove transform if necessary, or restructure positioning.

title: top and right properties in media query have no effect because element is not positioned
claim: #dice-container is not absolutely positioned (no position property), yet in the max-width:600px media query, top:10px and right:10px are set, which have no effect.
evidence: Lines 70-82 define #dice-container without position; lines 185-190 in the media query set top:10px; right:10px.
trigger: Viewing on a screen ≤600px and expecting the dice to be positioned at top-right.
impact: The dice container does not move to the intended location; layout may remain default, causing unintended overlap or spacing.
test_implication: Responsive testing should verify dice positioning.
suggested_verification: Inspect the computed style of #dice-container on a small screen; top/right should be ignored.
suggested_fix: Add position:absolute (and possibly adjust parent positioning) or remove the ineffective top/right if not needed.

title: Commentary panel scrolling is disabled due to pointer-events:none and missing height constraint
claim: #right-commentary-panel has pointer-events:none, which prevents any mouse interaction including scrolling with the wheel or scrollbar. Additionally, #commentary-content has flex:1 but its parent is not a flex container, and it has no height constraint, so overflow-y:auto will never activate a scrollbar.
evidence: Line 290 sets pointer-events:none on the panel. Line 294 sets flex:1 on #commentary-content but #right-commentary-panel is not display:flex. Lines 295-296 set overflow-y:auto and padding, but without a constrained height, the content element grows to fit its content, so no overflow occurs.
trigger: When commentary content exceeds the panel's height.
impact: Users cannot scroll to see all commentary; content may be clipped by the parent's overflow:hidden, making some text inaccessible.
test_implication: Testing with long commentary text should verify scrolling functionality.
suggested_verification: Insert enough commentary to overflow the panel and attempt to scroll with mouse wheel and scrollbar.
suggested_fix: Remove pointer-events:none from the panel (or set it only on non-scrollable parts) and add either display:flex to the panel or set height:100% (or max-height:100%) on #commentary-content.

title: Active player name color selector likely does not match actual DOM structure
claim: The CSS tries to color the active player's name using a span selector (#player-info div.active-player span:nth-child(2)), but the player info items are likely built with div elements (as evidenced by earlier selectors like #player-info div div div:nth-child(2)), so the style will not apply.
evidence: Lines 117-121 style '#player-info div div div:nth-child(2)' as the name; line 137-138 targets 'span:nth-child(2)' inside .active-player. If the markup uses divs, the span selector fails.
trigger: When a player is active and the active-player class is applied.
impact: The active player's name will not be highlighted in yellow, reducing visual clarity.
test_implication: Add a test to verify that the active player's name is styled correctly.
suggested_verification: Inspect the DOM of the player info panel and check the computed color of the name element when active.
suggested_fix: Change the selector to #player-info div.active-player div:nth-child(2) (or use a more specific class) to match the actual markup, or update the markup to use spans consistently.

title: Fixed 380px board size may overflow its container on small screens
claim: #game-board has a fixed width and height of 380px, which does not scale with the available space in #game-board-container. On narrow screens, the container may be less than 380px wide, causing overflow.
evidence: Lines 52-53 set width:380px; height:380px. The parent #game-board-container has flex:1 and can shrink, but the board does not.
trigger: Viewing the game on a screen where the flex container for the board is narrower than 380px.
impact: The board may overflow horizontally, causing layout breakage and potential overlap with other panels.
test_implication: Responsive testing should include board scaling.
suggested_verification: Reduce viewport width and observe if the board overflows its container.
suggested_fix: Make the board responsive, e.g., width:100%; height:auto; (with appropriate aspect ratio) or use max-width:100% and max-height with object-fit.

title: Duplicate selector definitions for #game-board-container lead to maintainability issues
claim: #game-board-container is defined twice: first at lines 249-251 with flex:1 1 auto, then again at lines 275-278 with flex:1 and position:relative. The second definition overrides the first, but having two separate blocks for the same selector makes the CSS harder to maintain and understand.
trigger: Future modifications to the board container may inadvertently change one definition without noticing the other.
impact: Increased risk of inconsistent styling and confusion.
test_implication: No functional test impact, but code review should catch duplicates.
suggested_fix: Merge the properties into a single #game-board-container rule.
